svg.title: A screenshot of the integrate demo beside the measured per-step cost
svg.desc: The phase plot shows a red spiral leaving the panel while green and violet trace a single closed curve on the exact orbit, and the energy chart shows red climbing as a straight line on a log axis while the others stay flat.
svg.text: demos/integrate, six simulated seconds, h = 1/60, ω = 2π
The red spiral leaves the panel after four
seconds and is CLIPPED, not rescaled — the
view follows the worst track only up to
three amplitudes. Without that ceiling the
picture ends up showing nothing but the
thing that is broken.
Green and violet are INDISTINGUISHABLE here,
and so is the pale shadow ellipse under them.
That is the result, not a rendering fault:
at hω = 0.105 the ellipse is 2.7% off a
circle and both rules are sitting on it.
Right: the same run as energy, log₁₀, against
a flat line at 1. Straight = exponential.
I.1 ns / body / step
cost
force evals
explicit Euler
semi-implicit
velocity Verlet
control, walking the array only: 0.608 ns
The two Euler rules agree to 3%, against a
run-to-run spread of the same size. Same
cost. One of them is wrong at every h.
